content.value_statement: Inconsistent markup causes accessibility, usability, and search problems. This skill guides you toward semantic structure, resilient forms, and useful document metadata.
actual_capabilities: Select semantic landmarks, headings, lists, tables, figures, and disclosure elements.
Design labeled forms with suitable input types, autocomplete, grouping, and native validation.
Apply accessible interaction patterns using native controls and focused ARIA attributes.
Recommend document language, viewport, title, description, canonical, social, and structured-data metadata.
Suggest image dimensions, loading behavior, script loading, and resource hints for stable pages.
limitations: It does not create CSS layouts, visual themes, or complete interface designs.
It does not implement JavaScript behavior or validate a running application.
It provides guidance rather than checking every browser, assistive technology, or search engine.
It cannot replace manual accessibility testing with keyboards and assistive technologies.

use_cases.title: Start a new page
use_cases.description: Generate a semantic document skeleton with landmarks, headings, metadata, and accessible content structure.

use_cases.title: Improve a form
use_cases.description: Review fields, labels, input types, grouping, validation, and error associations for a more usable form.

use_cases.title: Audit markup quality
use_cases.description: Inspect existing HTML for semantic, accessibility, metadata, and performance-aware markup improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Create a page structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a semantic HTML structure for a page about [topic]. Include landmarks, a logical heading order, and accessible navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Build an accessible form
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the HTML for a [form type]. Include labels, suitable input types, autocomplete values, field grouping, native validation, and accessible error references.

prompt_templates.title: Review existing markup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HTML for semantic structure and accessibility. List each issue, explain its user impact, and propose a specific markup correction: [paste HTML].

prompt_templates.title: Optimize document metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the document head for [page type]. Recommend title, description, language, viewport, canonical, social metadata, structured data, image dimensions, and script loading improvements.

output_examples.input: How should a product page organize its main regions?
output_examples.output: Use one main landmark with a descriptive heading. Place site navigation in a nav landmark, supporting content in an aside, and related page content in sections or articles.

output_examples.input: What should I check on a newsletter signup form?
output: Give the email field a visible label and use the email input type.
Add autocomplete for email, native required validation, and an error message connected with an accessible description.
Use a submit button and preserve a visible focus state.

best_practices: Prefer native HTML elements before adding ARIA roles or custom interaction.
Give every control a clear label, suitable type, and predictable keyboard behavior.
Keep document structure, metadata, and resource loading aligned with the page purpose.
anti_patterns: Do not use clickable div elements when a button or link provides the required behavior.
Do not use placeholders as the only form labels or skip heading levels for visual styling.
Do not add aggressive alerts, unnecessary preload hints, or metadata without a clear purpose.

faq.question: Does this skill create CSS?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on semantic markup, native behavior, accessibility, forms, metadata, and performance-aware HTML.

faq.question: Can it design accessible forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers labels, input types, autocomplete, fieldsets, legends, native validation, and error associations.

faq.question: Does it replace an accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It provides markup guidance, but automated checks and manual testing remain necessary.

faq.question: Can it improve SEO markup?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend titles, descriptions, canonical links, social metadata, structured data, and semantic content structure.

faq.question: Should I use ARIA everywhere?
faq.answer: No. Prefer native semantics and add ARIA only when it fills a genuine accessibility gap.

faq.question: Can it review existing HTML?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the markup and context, and it can identify structural, form, metadata, and accessibility improvements.
